headline: Sunday morning: Dhaka ranks world's third most polluted city

headline_marked: Tennessee [[prison chief resigns]] after botched execution
headline: Tennessee prison chief resigns after botched execution
summary: Frank Strada steps down as Correction Department commissioner after a failed lethal injection attempt left a convicted murderer gravely ill.
details: The head of the Tennessee Department of Correction, Frank Strada, will resign this month following a failed attempt to execute convicted murderer Christa Pike.
The botched execution on Wednesday left Pike unconscious, intubated, and dependent on a mechanical ventilator to breathe.
This marks the state's second failed execution attempt this year, prompting Governor Bill Lee to halt all death penalty executions until the end of 2026.
Governor Lee has ordered an independent review of the incident, which took place at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville.
Pike's lawyers claim officials ignored medical warnings about her blood disorder and small veins, which made placing intravenous lines extremely difficult.
Pike, 50, was convicted three decades ago for the torture and killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in 1995.
Medical staff are currently working to clear the drug pentobarbital from her system and save her life.
caption:
A failed lethal injection left a prisoner unconscious and on a ventilator. Now, the state's prison chief has resigned.

The head of the Tennessee Department of Correction, Frank Strada, will resign this month following a failed attempt to execute convicted murderer Christa Pike.

The botched execution on Wednesday left Pike unconscious, intubated, and dependent on a mechanical ventilator to breathe.

This marks the state's second failed execution attempt this year, prompting Governor Bill Lee to halt all death penalty executions until the end of 2026.

Governor Lee has ordered an independent review of the incident, which took place at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville.

Pike's lawyers claim officials ignored medical warnings about her blood disorder and small veins, which made placing intravenous lines extremely difficult.

Pike, 50, was convicted three decades ago for the torture and killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in 1995.

Medical staff are currently working to clear the drug pentobarbital from her system and save her life.
